title: Module Hom comparison through a coefficient mate
statement:
Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal D$ be monoidal categories [def-sfb-monoidal-category]. Let $F:\mathcal C\rightleftarrows\mathcal D:G$ be a monoidal adjunction $F\dashv G$ with unit $u$ and counit $v$: $F$ is strong monoidal, $G$ is lax monoidal with tensor comparison $\mu^G$, and their monoidal structures are mates [def-sfb-modobj-transport-adjunction]. Let $B$ and $A$ be monoid objects in $\mathcal C$ and $\mathcal D$, respectively [sk-def-sfb-ring-object], and let $\alpha:FB\to A$ be a morphism of monoid objects. Set
$$\eta=G(\alpha)\circ u_B:B\longrightarrow GA.$$
Use module objects [sk-def-sfb-module-objects], transport $\operatorname{mapMod}$ [def-sfb-modobj-transport], and scalar restriction [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars]. Assume scalar extension along $\alpha$ is defined with value $A\otimes_{FB}-$ and with its extension/restriction adjunction as in [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars]. Then $\eta$ is a morphism of monoid objects, and there is a natural isomorphism
$$\theta:\operatorname{Res}_{u_B}\circ\operatorname{mapMod}(G)\circ\operatorname{Res}_{\alpha}\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Res}_{\eta}\circ\operatorname{mapMod}(G)$$
whose component and inverse on every $A$-module $N$ have underlying map $1_{GN}$: $\theta$ is the inverse of the isomorphism of [def-sfb-comap-mapmod-square] for the lax monoidal functor $G$ and the commutative square of monoid morphisms with $R_Y=S_Y=B$, $\varphi_Y=1_B$, $R_X=FB$, $S_X=A$, $\varphi_X=\alpha$, $\eta_R=u_B$ and $\eta_S=\eta$ (the square commutes by the definition of $\eta$), with $\operatorname{Res}_{1_B}$ the identity. More precisely the two actions on $GN$ coincide, with common action
$$G(\gamma_N)\circ\mu^G_{A,N}\circ(\eta\otimes1_{GN})
=G(\gamma_N)\circ G(\alpha\otimes1_N)\circ\mu^G_{FB,N}\circ(u_B\otimes1_{GN}).$$
For every $B$-module $M$ and $A$-module $N$ there is a natural bijection
$$\Hom_A\bigl(A\otimes_{FB}FM,N\bigr)\cong\Hom_B\bigl(M,\operatorname{Res}_{\eta}\operatorname{mapMod}(G)N\bigr).$$
Under this bijection a morphism $t:A\otimes_{FB}FM\to N$ has underlying adjunct $G(\widetilde t)\circ u_M$, where $\widetilde t:FM\to N$ is the $FB$-linear morphism corresponding to $t$ under extension/restriction of scalars. The inverse sends a $B$-linear $s:M\to GN$ to the $A$-linear morphism corresponding to $v_N\circ F(s):FM\to N$ under that same scalar adjunction. This is the adjunction $\operatorname{Ext}_{\alpha}\operatorname{mapMod}(F)\dashv\operatorname{Res}_{\eta}\operatorname{mapMod}(G)$ obtained from the lifted monoidal adjunction and the scalar adjunction, with the right adjoint identified by $\theta$. No invertibility of $\alpha$ is assumed.

proof.text: The unit $u_B:B\to GFB$ is a monoid morphism by [def-sfb-modobj-transport-adjunction]. Clause 1 of [det-def-sfb-ring-object-transport], applied to the lax monoidal functor $G$ and the monoid morphism $\alpha:FB\to A$, says that $G\alpha:GFB\to GA$ is a monoid morphism. Their composite $\eta=G\alpha\circ u_B$ is therefore a monoid morphism: its unit equation is the composite of their unit equations, and its multiplication equation follows by substituting their multiplication equations and using $(G\alpha\otimes G\alpha)\circ(u_B\otimes u_B)=(G\alpha\circ u_B)\otimes(G\alpha\circ u_B)$, by bifunctoriality. These are exactly the morphism conditions of [sk-def-sfb-ring-object].

source.place: sole paragraph: coefficient-mate identification and composition of adjunctions

proof.text:
For an $A$-module $N$ with action $\gamma_N$, restriction and transport give the two $B$-actions on $GN$, by [def-sfb-modobj-restriction] and [def-sfb-modobj-transport]:
$$a_N=G(\gamma_N)\circ G(\alpha\otimes1_N)\circ\mu^G_{FB,N}\circ(u_B\otimes1_{GN}),\qquad b_N=G(\gamma_N)\circ\mu^G_{A,N}\circ(\eta\otimes1_{GN}).$$
Naturality of the lax tensor maps, explicitly part of [det-def-sfb-ring-object-transport], gives
$$G(\alpha\otimes1_N)\circ\mu^G_{FB,N}=\mu^G_{A,N}\circ(G\alpha\otimes1_{GN}).$$
Substitute this in $a_N$ and combine the two tensor factors by bifunctoriality. Since $G\alpha\circ u_B=\eta$, the result is $b_N$, proving the displayed common-action identity. This uses no inverse tensor map for $G$.

source.place: sole paragraph: coefficient-mate identification and composition of adjunctions

proof.text: Apply [def-sfb-comap-mapmod-square] to $G$, with $R_Y=S_Y=B$, $\varphi_Y=1_B$, $R_X=FB$, $S_X=A$, $\varphi_X=\alpha$, $\eta_R=u_B$ and $\eta_S=\eta$. Step 1 supplies the required monoid morphisms, and the square equation is $\eta\circ1_B=G\alpha\circ u_B$. The square isomorphism goes from $\operatorname{Res}_{\eta}\operatorname{mapMod}(G)$ to $\operatorname{Res}_{u_B}\operatorname{mapMod}(G)\operatorname{Res}_{\alpha}$, after removing restriction along $1_B$. That removal has underlying identity, since its action is $\gamma\circ(1_B\otimes1)=\gamma$ by [def-sfb-modobj-restriction]. Take the inverse of this specified isomorphism to obtain $\theta$ in the required direction. Its original components have underlying identity by [lem-sfb-comap-mapmod-square-underlying]. Their inverses also have underlying identity: composition of module maps is ambient composition by [sk-def-sfb-module-objects], so the inverse equation reads $h\circ1=1$, hence $h=1$. Thus $\theta$ and $\theta^{-1}$ have the claimed underlying maps; step 2 identifies their source and target actions explicitly.

source.place: sole paragraph: square comparison through the common composite; inverse for the coefficient-mate square

proof.text:
Write $T=\operatorname{mapMod}(F)$, $R=\operatorname{Res}_{u_B}\operatorname{mapMod}(G)$, $E=\operatorname{Ext}_{\alpha}$ and $S=\operatorname{Res}_{\alpha}$. The lifted adjunction $T\dashv R$ is [def-sfb-modobj-transport-adjunction]. The hypothesis supplies $E\dashv S$ with the tensor value and scalar Hom bijection of clause 2 of [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars]; no existence of scalar extension in an arbitrary monoidal category is being inferred. By [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction], their composite has Hom bijection
$$\Hom_A(ETM,N)\cong\Hom_{FB}(TM,SN)\cong\Hom_B(M,RSN).$$
Postcompose the final morphism with $\theta_N:RSN\to\operatorname{Res}_{\eta}\operatorname{mapMod}(G)N$. This is a further bijection, with inverse given by postcomposition with $\theta_N^{-1}$. All three bijections are natural in $M$ and $N$: the first two are adjunction bijections, and for the last, precomposition commutes with postcomposition by associativity, while naturality in $N$ is the naturality equation for $\theta$. They therefore give the stated adjunction by [lem-weil-pbc-adjunction-of-natural-bijection], with left adjoint $ET$ and the specified right adjoint. This is precisely the composite adjunction with its right adjoint identified by $\theta$.

source.place: sole paragraph: coefficient-mate identification and composition of adjunctions

proof.text: Let $t:ETM\to N$ correspond under $E\dashv S$ to $\widetilde t:FM\to\operatorname{Res}_{\alpha}N$. The lifted Hom bijection is the underlying bijection of $F\dashv G$ by [def-sfb-modobj-transport-adjunction]. Its unit formula from [lem-weil-pbc-adjunction-of-natural-bijection] is therefore $G(\widetilde t)\circ u_M$. Postcomposing with $\theta_N$ leaves that underlying arrow unchanged by step 3. Conversely, first postcompose a $B$-linear $s:M\to\operatorname{Res}_{\eta}\operatorname{mapMod}(G)N$ with $\theta_N^{-1}$, which again leaves the underlying arrow unchanged. The inverse lifted bijection gives the $FB$-linear map with underlying arrow $v_N\circ F(s)$, by the counit formula in [lem-weil-pbc-adjunction-of-natural-bijection]. Finally apply the inverse scalar Hom bijection of clause 2 of [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars] to obtain the claimed $A$-linear map. These operations are inverse because each is one of the three bijections of step 4 or its inverse. No step uses invertibility of $\alpha$.

The delivery is one commit with the report and the item and adds no new nodes. The statement and stmt_deps are identical to the live node, which is still unsplit, so no other group has done this split. The route matches def-sfb-module-upper-lower-adjunction.proof.md in main-20261015 (lift the monoidal adjunction, compose with the scalar adjunction, identify the right adjoint through η=Gα∘u). Step 1: η is a monoid morphism because u_B is one by the statement of def-sfb-modobj-transport-adjunction, Gα is one by clause 1 of det-def-sfb-ring-object-transport, and composites of monoid morphisms are monoid morphisms; this is correctly marked elementary. Step 2: I recomputed both actions from def-sfb-modobj-restriction and def-sfb-modobj-transport. They agree by naturality of μ^G, which the statement of det-def-sfb-ring-object-transport gives. Step 3: I matched def-sfb-comap-mapmod-square with the categories swapped (φ_X=α, φ_Y=1_B, η_R=u_B, η_S=η). θ is the inverse of that square isomorphism, so the direction is right. The underlying identity comes from the statement of lem-sfb-comap-mapmod-square-underlying, and the inverse has underlying identity because the forgetful functor is a functor. Step 4: the composite adjunction ET⊣RS, then postcomposition with θ. Both naturality checks hold, and the adjunction follows from lem-weil-pbc-adjunction-of-natural-bijection, a Mathlib leaf. The scalar adjunction comes from the item's explicit hypothesis, not from the braided/commutative conditions of clause 2 of sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars. That reading is correct because FB need not be commutative. Step 5: the Hom formulas Ψ=G(−)∘u and Ψ⁻¹=v∘F(−) are correct, and θ^{±1} leave the underlying arrows unchanged. Small cases checked: F=G=id, α=id, and Z→Z/2 with α not invertible. No step inverts α or μ^G. No duplicates: def-sfb-module-upper-lower-adjunction is the condensed special case and the only citer, and lem-sfb-eta-ring-hom is the special case of step 1 for η_f. No SGA source and no tool_uses needed.
